results.title: Fifi Kwetey admits political mercenaries exist within NDC
results.content: The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, has acknowledged that political mercenaries operate within Ghana's political parties, including his own, warning that the practice undermines party discipline and national development. Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said many people join political parties primarily for personal benefits rather than a commitment to the ideals and objectives of the organisations. "A mercenary is somebody who is literally in it just for himself. If he gets his benefit, he can motivate everybody because all he wants is himself. results.title: IGNITE, brAInify train 50 police and immigration officers in AI
results.content: Fifty officers from the Ghana Police Service's Criminal Investigations Department (CID) and the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) have received specialised training in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to support criminal investigations and intelligence gathering. The training, organised by IGNITE Social Enterprise in partnership with brAInify, took place in Accra on October 29, 2026. It brought together senior personnel from the two security agencies, including officers from the CID's Anti-Human Trafficking Unit, Interpol, Cybersecurity, Financial Crime and Legal units. The programme focused on practical applications of AI in managing complex case files, analysing financial transaction trails, identifying manipulated digital content and preparing intelligence reports for command-level decision-making. results.title: When applause replaces discernment
results.content: There is something about the recent exchanges among some prominent Ghanaian religious leaders that deserves more attention than it is receiving. The focus has largely been on what one pastor said about other prophets, who has responded, who has taken offence and who has insulted whom. But I believe we are overlooking an equally important part of the story: the people sitting in the congregations, listening, clapping, cheering and sometimes appearing visibly delighted as their pastors attack fellow ministers from the pulpit.

results.title: Connecting Africa’s wallets, unlocking Africa’s trade, smartly
results.content: Yesterday, Monday, 2 November, I joined discussions at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra, including a Smart Africa Steering Committee roundtable. My main message was that connecting Africa’s mobile money wallets across borders, alongside visa-free travel, could transform intra-African trade, significantly. At the Africa Prosperity Network (APN), we estimate that implementing both reforms could help raise intra-African trade from around 16% to more than 25% within five years. The opportunity is enormous. The figures I presented show that US$2.1 trillion flowed through mobile money wallets globally in 2025, with approximately US$1.4 trillion, two-thirds of the total, transacted in sub-Saharan Africa. results.title: GIS investigates explosion that killed officer during Hamile border patrol
results.content: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is investigating an explosion during a border patrol operation in the Hamile Sector of the Upper West Region that killed one of its officers and a tricycle rider. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, along an unapproved route in the border area, according to a statement issued by the Service. The GIS said a team of four officers on patrol responded to an unusual sound and intercepted a man transporting a load on a tricycle. The rider reportedly attempted to flee as the officers approached to inspect the contents of the load. “In the process of trying to stop him, the load exploded, resulting in the death of the tricycle rider and injuries to two officers,” the statement said.

results.title: Deputy Works Minister urges business leaders to strengthen project delivery accountability
results.content: Deputy Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources, Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, has urged chief executives and business leaders to strengthen project planning, leadership accountability and implementation oversight to improve the delivery of development projects. She said successful project delivery required more than initiating projects, stressing the importance of adequate preparation, clearly defined responsibilities and continuous monitoring. Speaking at the PM Executive Summit organised by the Project Management Institute (PMI), she urged institutions to identify potential risks early, track project milestones and address implementation challenges before they escalated. "One of the most important responsibilities of leadership is to establish a culture in which commitments are matched by action and performance is assessed against clear standards," she said.

results.title: The world has not had a single cooler-than-normal day since December 2022
results.content: The last time the planet's average temperature dipped below normal was 1 December 2022, and even then only by 0.006°C, a difference far too small to feel. Every day since, from 2 December 2022 to 26 October 2026, has been warmer than normal for its date.

results.title: When Men of God begin exposing God’s Men!
results.content: Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, a respected pastor raised concerns about the activities of false prophets, and before the congregation could finish saying Amen, another man of God had reportedly begun preparing to open the archives of embarrassing secrets. What started as a general sermon about questionable spiritual practices soon produced a remarkably personal response, complete with warnings about information that could allegedly embarrass prominent religious personalities. For a country that has spent years complaining about unemployment, this was encouraging news. The religious industry had apparently created a new profession: Prophetic Intelligence Officer, specialising in the collection, preservation and strategic release of confidential information about fellow servants of God.
